newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Teck Corp says may stand aside on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Teck Corp says may stand aside on Busang.

text.p: Teck Corp president Norman Keevil said on Thursday the company would not participate in the huge Busang gold find unless invited by the Indonesian government.
"If the government invites us to be a participant in the process, we would be happy to be there. If they don't invite us, we will stand aside," Keevil told Reuters in Jakarta.
"We don't want to interfere with things. It's up to the Indonesian government to decide what it wants to do. If it wants to open the process up, then we will be happy to be a part of it," he said.

"The government has said Bre-X (Minerals Ltd) should negotiate with Barrick (Gold Corp) and until such time as they say that Bre-X is free to negotiate with people, we will keep talking but cannot negotiate," he said.
Teck senior vice-president Mike Lipkewich said in Vancouver on Wednesday the company and Newmont Mining Corp were discussing a joint bid for the Busang property.
"We are very interested in the property. We have had numerous serious discussions with Bre-X. We are looking at it very seriously," Lipkewich told Reuters.
Keevil confirmed holding talks with Bre-X, but added the Busang situation had changed since November, when the Indonesian government picked Barrick to partner Bre-X to develop the find.
"Where it (Busang) stands now is not too clear to me, and probably not to anybody. The situation is very foggy out there. I can hear two fog horns, but I am not sure who they are."
Keevil said he was not at liberty to discuss Teck's proposal to Bre-X, adding that making it public "would be seen as interfering with the process".
He declined to say if he had met with Indonesian government officials during his visit to Jakarta, but said he had not met with influential Indonesian businessman Muhammad "Bob" Hasan.
Hasan has taken a 50-percent stake in PT Askatinto Karya Mineral, which has a 10-percent share in the richest parts of the property, Busang II and III.

John Willson, president of Placer Dome Inc, which has proposed a $5 billion merger with Bre-X to jointly develop the property, said last week he had held talks with Hasan, a close associate of President Suharto.
